inline.s: Gather in all six sense-roots, and let pure thought succeed without break.
Question: What is gathering the mind in Buddha-recitation?
Answer: To gather the mind is to cause the mind to focus on a single object, neither scattered nor drowsy.
Therefore gathering the mind in Buddha-recitation is single-minded Buddha-recitation.
The Great Master Yinguang instructed:
“Gathering the mind in Buddha-recitation is the certain and unchanging Way.”
(The Collected Writings of Master Yinguang
First Letter in Reply to the Layman Liu Guanshan.) The Great Master Yinguang further instructed:
“As for reciting the Buddha, when the mind is hard to unify — apply gathered, earnest recitation, and it will of itself unify.”
(The Collected Writings of Master Yinguang
Fourth Letter in Reply to the Layman Gao Shaolin.)
The Great Master Yinguang instructed:

“Of the Mahayana sutras that speak of the Pure Land in passing, there are numerous beyond counting. And the Chapter on the Perfect Penetration of the Mahasthamaprapta’s Buddha-Recitation in the Surangama Sutra
is in truth the most wonderful instruction on Buddha-recitation

. If sentient beings can recite with ‘gathering in all six sense-roots, and pure thought continuing without break,’ how could they fail in the present life or in the future to certainly see the Buddha, closely realize perfect penetration, and far achieve the Buddha-way!”
(Preface to the Reprint of the Five Pure Land Sutras.)

[Five Pure Land Sutras]To the Three Pure Land Sutras are added the Aspiration and Practice Vows of the Bodhisattva Universal Worthy and the Chapter on the Perfect Penetration of the Mahasthamaprapta’s Buddha-Recitation; together these are called the Five Pure Land Sutras. [Three Pure Land Sutras]The three scriptures on which the Pure Land school relies: the Sutra of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life Spoken by the Buddha, the Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life Spoken by the Buddha, and the Amitābha Sutra Spoken by the Buddha.
The Great Master Yinguang further instructed:
“As a child remembers its mother, so remember the World-Honored One
(Amitābha Buddha)
, and at once you receive grace. When the causal mind and the fruit-enlightenment respond to each other, you immediately return to the source; gathering in the six roots — its wonder cannot be told.”
(In Praise of the Mahasthamaprapta.)

[Causal mind]The mind of the causal ground; here it refers to the sentient being’s mind of remembering the Buddha. [Causal ground and fruit ground]From the first rousing of the mind to study Buddhism as an ordinary being, up until just before the perfect achievement of Buddhahood, this whole process is called the “causal ground”; the perfect achievement of Buddhahood is called the fruit ground. [Fruit-enlightenment]The enlightenment of the fruit ground; here it refers to the complete great enlightenment of Amitābha Buddha.
Therefore, a person who recites the Buddha must gather the mind in Buddha-recitation (single-minded Buddha-recitation),
so as to ensure that at death the ten thoughts continue without break
, and so be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
On this, the Great Master Tanluan, the Great Master Daochuo, the Great Master Shandao, and the Great Master Yongming all have clear instructions.

The Great Master Tanluan and the Great Master Daochuo are sages who have realized the fruit, and the Great Master Shandao and the Great Master Yongming are incarnations of Amitābha Buddha; their words are the
measure of the holy word
[Measure of the holy word]This is what the sages have spoken, correct and without error, and certainly to be believed and received.
The Great Master Tanluan instructed
(see
The Pure Land Teaching of the Great Master Tanluan
With no other mind intruding, thought following thought
(continuing without break)
, up to ten thoughts — this is called the ten thoughts continuing without break.
If at death the ten thoughts continue without break, one gains rebirth.
The Great Master Daochuo instructed
(see
The Pure Land Teaching of the Great Master Daochuo
If there is a sentient being, even if throughout his life he commits evil,
yet at the end of life, ten thoughts continuing without break,
calls upon my name —
if he is not reborn, may I not attain right enlightenment.
The Great Master Shandao, an incarnation of Amitābha Buddha, instructed
(see
The Pure Land Teaching of the Great Master Shandao
Continuous recitation brings rebirth.
If one can
practice thought after thought continuing without break
(pure thought continuing without break)
taking the end of life as the limit
for one who does so
, then of ten, ten are reborn; of a hundred, a hundred are reborn.
If I attain Buddhahood, and sentient beings of the ten directions call upon my name, aspiring to be born in my land,
down to ten thoughts
(down to ten thoughts continuing without break at death)
, if they are not reborn, may I not attain right enlightenment.
[Continuous recitation brings rebirth]
At the moment of death, if one only makes the thought of Buddha-recitation continue without break (not interrupted by deluded thoughts), one gains rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[Down to ten thoughts]
The “down to ten thoughts” spoken of here, taken together with the above instruction of the Great Master Shandao —
‘precisely because calling upon the Name is easy, continuous recitation brings rebirth. If one can
practice thought after thought continuing without break, taking the end of life as the limit
, then of ten, ten are reborn; of a hundred, a hundred are reborn.’
— one can clearly see that this is
an abbreviated way of saying ‘up to the whole of one life
(one lifetime)
of thought after thought continuing without break, and down to
ten thoughts continuing without break at death
, because the Great Master Shandao has already clearly said:
‘Thought after thought continuing without break, taking the end of life as the limit.’
And
‘thought after thought continuing without break, taking the end of life as the limit’
is precisely in order to make one’s thought after thought continuing without break, so that the practiced habit becomes second nature,
so as to ensure the ten thoughts continuing without break at death
If one recites the Buddha in ordinary times but does not recite at death, or recites at death but with a scattered mind, then this is not
‘thought after thought continuing without break, taking the end of life as the limit’
. Therefore, the meaning of ‘down to ten thoughts’ is
‘down to ten thoughts continuing without break at death’
. This concise rhetorical device is found everywhere in classical prose. Therefore
‘down to ten thoughts, if not reborn, may I not attain right enlightenment’
means precisely:
ten thoughts at death, continuing without break, bring rebirth.
[Ten thoughts]Reciting ten phrases of the Buddha's name.
[Thought after thought continuing without break, practiced habit becomes nature]Through repeated practice, making thought after thought continuous become habitual.

The Great Master Shandao is an incarnation of Amitābha Buddha, and his words are the words of Amitābha Buddha. How one can be reborn is of course to be taken on the authority of his words — this is the measure of the holy word. A person who recites the Buddha must engrave it on his heart, believing it ever more deeply, and relying on it ever more surely.

Note: In the era of the Great Master Shandao, through the teaching of these three generations of patriarchs — the Great Master Tanluan, the Great Master Daochuo, and the Great Master Shandao — that the ten thoughts continuing without break at death are the condition for rebirth had already become the common understanding of the Buddha-reciting people of that time, and was their most basic common knowledge.
Therefore
‘down to ten thoughts, if not reborn, may I not attain right enlightenment’
clearly means:
ten thoughts at death, continuing without break, bring rebirth.
Unless one is a complete ignoramus wholly ignorant of the matter, or a malicious slanderer of the Dharma with ulterior motives, one would never go so far as to twist
‘down to ten thoughts, if not reborn, may I not attain right enlightenment’

into ‘reciting the Buddha with a scattered mind in ordinary times for ten phrases, one gains rebirth.’ Therefore the Great Master Shandao adopted the concise expression ‘down to ten thoughts,’ making the whole sentence concise and neat, pleasant to read aloud, and easy to memorize.
Moreover the Great Master Shandao clearly stated:
‘Continuous recitation brings rebirth. If one can
practice thought after thought continuing without break, taking the end of life as the limit
, then of ten, ten are reborn; of a hundred, a hundred are reborn.
I wish that all people would think this over well: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one must
sharpen the mind and discipline oneself
(rouse oneself and restrain oneself)
forgoing neither by day nor by night
(neither by day nor by night ceasing from thought after thought continuing without break)
; when the previous thought ends, the next thought immediately arises, forever enjoying the Dharma-joy of the unconditioned, even to the attainment of Buddhahood — how joyful it would be!’
(See
The Pure Land Teaching of the Great Master Shandao
If ‘reciting the Buddha in ordinary times with a scattered mind for ten phrases, one gains rebirth’ were the case, then what need would there be for
‘thought after thought continuing without break, taking the end of life as the limit’
? And what need for
‘whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one must sharpen the mind and discipline oneself, forgoing neither by day nor by night’
? Therefore the twisting by Huijing, Jingzong, and others of
‘down to ten thoughts, if not reborn, may I not attain right enlightenment’

into ‘reciting the Buddha with a scattered mind in ordinary times for ten phrases, one gains rebirth’ (and their consequent noisy promotion of ‘calling the name surely brings rebirth’) is entirely wrong.
The Great Master Yongming, an incarnation of Amitābha Buddha, instructed
The Collection of All Good Converging to the One
Now is the cause; death is the fruit
. One should make the cause real, and the fruit will not be empty. If one wishes
the ten thoughts at death to be accomplished
(if one wishes to accomplish the ten thoughts continuing without break at death)
, then one must
prepare in advance the crossing
(that is, make full preparation in advance)
; gather together one’s merit and dedicate it to this time
(dedicate it to the time of death)
; thought after thought without failing
(thought after thought continuing without break)
, then there will be no worry.
[The ten thoughts at death accomplished]To accomplish the ten thoughts continuing without break at death. (See the essay
“At Death, Ten Thoughts Continuing Without Break Bring Rebirth”
.) [But preparing in advance the crossing]Is to make full preparation in advance. “Crossing”: a ferry and a bridge. “Preparing in advance the crossing” means making full preparation in advance.
Śākyamuni Buddha instructed
The Sutra of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life Spoken by the Buddha
Though one toils hard for a whole lifetime, in a short while afterwards one is born in the Land of Immeasurable Life, with happiness without limit.
